meiji_transition.summary: Kagawa Prefecture was set up in 1871, merged into Myōdō in 1873, restored in 1875, merged into Ehime in 1876, and set up for the third time in 1888.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Kagawa = Sanuki Province, Japan's smallest prefecture; it was merged away and restored three times in the Meiji era before becoming independent for good in 1888.

history_timeline.title: Kūkai's birthplace
history_timeline.summary: Kūkai (Kōbō Daishi) was born near Zentsū-ji in Sanuki; in 821 he led the repair of the Mannō Pond.

history_timeline.title: The vengeful spirit of Sutoku
history_timeline.summary: After the Hōgen Rebellion Retired Emperor Sutoku was exiled to Sanuki and died there, becoming a famous vengeful spirit; in the Kamakura period Sanuki was ruled by shogunal vassals.

history_timeline.title: Domain of the Hosokawa kanrei
history_timeline.summary: Sanuki was ruled directly by the Keichō Hosokawa, the kanrei house, with the 'four guardians of the Hosokawa' — the Kagawa, Kōzai, Yasutomi and others — as deputies.

history_timeline.title: The Chōsokabe invasion
history_timeline.summary: Sanuki's local lords allied with the Miyoshi; in the 1580s Chōsokabe Motochika swallowed Sanuki, which Hideyoshi took back in his Shikoku campaign.

history_timeline.title: The Konpira pilgrimage
history_timeline.summary: Takamatsu (Matsudaira) and Marugame (Kyōgoku) split the province; the 'Konpira pilgrimage' rivaled the Ise pilgrimage as a common dream, and the 'three whites of Sanuki' — salt, sugar and cotton — underpinned the economy.

history_timeline.title: Great Seto Bridge
history_timeline.summary: The Great Seto Bridge opened in 1988, linking Shikoku to Honshū; Kagawa styles itself 'Udon Prefecture' after Sanuki udon.

specialties.name: Honetsuki-dori
specialties.note: Marugame's roast chicken leg on the bone

dialect.name: Sanuki dialect
dialect.features: Endings like '-ken' and '-mai'; 'mandegan' means everything, with an intonation close to Kansai's.

guide.opening: I'm a pilgrim — Master Kūkai was born right here at Zentsū-ji. How about a bowl of udon first, and then I'll tell you how this prefecture was 'founded three times'?

regional_meme.title: Udon Prefecture
regional_meme.text: Kagawa once rebranded itself 'Udon Prefecture'; legend says udon broth flows from the taps here (some facilities really installed them).

regional_meme.title: The gaming ordinance
regional_meme.text: Kagawa passed an ordinance limiting how long children may play video games, sparking a nationwide debate.

hero_persona.name: Kūkai
hero_persona.title: Kōbō Daishi
hero_persona.opening_line: This humble monk is Kūkai, born in Sanuki. I went to Tang China to seek the Dharma and returned to found Shingon Buddhism — my footprints are at all eighty-eight temples of Shikoku.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: profound and compassionate, learned and versatile; speaks of the Dharma, calligraphy and engineering (the Mannō Pond)

ramen.highlight: Ramen keeps a low profile in Udon Prefecture — ask a local and they'll say 'go have udon instead'

sake.taste_profile: Rich & dry: a full-bodied pure-rice sake from the temple town of Konpira
